import cv2, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
im=cv2.imread('first_frame.png')
h,w=im.shape[:2]
Y,X=np.ogrid[:h,:w]
# broad union object and shadow
m1=((X-366)/58)**2+((Y-255)/55)**2<1
m2=((X-383)/84)**2+((Y-278)/34)**2<1
mask=np.where(m1|m2,255,0).astype(np.uint8)
for meth,nm in [(cv2.INPAINT_TELEA,'telea'),(cv2.INPAINT_NS,'ns')]:
 bg=cv2.inpaint(im,mask,7,meth)
 cv2.imwrite(f'.tmp/bg_{nm}.png',bg)
# horizontal linear per row based on robust left/right strips + noise from x+180
bg=im.copy().astype(float)
x0,x1=292,458
for y in range(185,330):
    # linear from means immediate ranges
    lv=np.median(im[y,270:292].astype(float),axis=0)
    rv=np.median(im[y,458:480].astype(float),axis=0)
    for x in range(x0,x1):
        t=(x-x0)/(x1-x0)
        base=lv*(1-t)+rv*t
        # texture from source x+250 highpassed by local row smooth-ish
        sx=min(w-1,x+250)
        raw=im[y,sx].astype(float)
        loc=np.mean(im[y,max(0,sx-15):min(w,sx+16)].astype(float),axis=0)
        bg[y,x]=np.clip(base+0.55*(raw-loc),0,255)
cv2.imwrite('.tmp/bg_linear.png',bg.astype(np.uint8))
PY
